name: travel-walk-v1
status: draft: defaults from research, not yet reviewed by the author
audience: a man (18–60+) scrolling Reels who stops for a pretty, self-ironic, flirty woman on a walk; women welcome but secondary
_doc: Pixel units: `canvas.width/height` are output pixels (2160x3840 by default, the author's preference since 2026-10-11). Every other pixel number in this file (safe_zone, overlay_positions, typography.*.size, animation.in.distance_px) and in overlays/src/presets.ts and slots.json is in a 1080-wide reference space (`canvas.reference_width`), so the numbers read as on a 1080x1920 frame. Canvas pixels = reference pixels x canvas.width / canvas.reference_width (x2 at 2160x3840). The overlay renderer (overlays/src/style.ts designScale) and cf.canvas (Python) apply that one factor. Named canvases: `canvases` holds one preset per orientation (portrait, landscape), each with its own size, reference_width and, where they differ from the top-level ones, safe_zone, overlay_positions and slots (all in that preset's reference space). `canvas` is the active default (portrait); a Script's top-level `canvas` ('landscape') picks a preset, and `--canvas landscape|portrait|WxH` on cf.build / cf.render / cf.render_check / overlays/render.mjs wins over both. `assets` holds the Library cue boxes, default positions, still lengths and the sound level rule (docs/script-schema.md, Assets).

canvas.note: Active default canvas (= canvases.portrait): 4K vertical (author, 2026-10-11). cf.build/cf.render take --canvas 1080x1920 for comparison renders, --canvas landscape (or a Script's canvas: 'landscape') for 16:9.

canvases._doc: Named canvas presets (cf.canvas.resolve, overlays/render.mjs). A preset without safe_zone / overlay_positions / slots uses the top-level ones (style.json safe_zone, overlay_positions, overlays/src/slots.json). A preset with overlay_positions has role_placement 'overlay_positions': every overlay preset (presets.ts) takes its anchor/x/y from there instead of its own portrait placement; font sizes, boxes and caps stay, so text is the same size relative to the frame's short side (designScale = width / reference_width = 2 on both 4K canvases). A WxH override picks the preset with the same aspect ratio.

portrait.note: 9:16 Reel; safe_zone, overlay_positions and slots are the top-level ones (Meta Reels UI).

landscape.note: 16:9 for YouTube and the Instagram feed (first horizontal video: reel-02-boat, 2026-10-11). Reference space 1920x1080, x2 at 3840x2160.

safe_zone.source: 5 % margins all round (title-safe for 16:9); bottom 12 % keeps text clear of the YouTube progress bar and player controls. No right rail: feed and YouTube put no buttons over a 16:9 frame.

slots._doc: Named placements for a spec's `anchor` on this canvas (same names as overlays/src/slots.json, 1920x1080 reference px). bottom-* y is the box's bottom edge at rest; the 24 px slide-in starts below it, so y <= 1080 - 130 - 24 = 926.

lower-left-loose._note: inside the 5 % frame margin but over the YouTube controls band (safe-zone warning); for the Instagram feed only

asset_pos._units: reference px (1920x1080); the Asset fits inside the box, centred

safe_zone.source: Meta Ads Guide 14% top / 35% bottom; sides 130 px, not Meta's 6% (65 px): Instagram on a tall phone (iPhone 19.5:9; her screenshot is 920x2000) shows a 9:16 Reel full-screen by height and crops (1 - (920/2000)/(9/16))/2 = 9.1% off each side, about 98 px at 1080; 98 px crop + 32 px margin = 130. Found on her post "Офис — нишевые слова для парня" (2026-10-19): the left edge of the list was cut off ('niche' lost its n, the numbers 1)-9) were cut)

typography.preset_note: overlay design system from overlays/src/presets.ts: legacy | editorial-serif | clean-grotesk | lower-third-tag | tiktok-hype | pinterest-aesthetic | coquette-girly | y2k-gloss | diary-typewriter | handwritten-note. Non-legacy presets override display/body, colors.text/backdrop and overlay_positions for overlays. Board: reels/reel-01/overlay-design/board.png
typography.font_note: Overlay font from the Library: an Asset ref '@font/<name>' (a .ttf/.otf in a Pack) or null. It replaces the font family of every overlay role (hook, place, fact, line) of whatever preset; sizes, case, boxes and positions stay. A Format's FORMAT.md line '- Overlay font: `@font/<name>`' wins over it. Resolved by python -m cf.assets font; overlays/render.mjs takes it as the spec's font_file (overlays/README.md).

color.rule: original colour, as on the Mac (author, 2026-10-12): no grade, no levelling, no Look
color.note: hdr_source 'apple-sdr': HDR clips (iPhone HLG / Dolby Vision) go into Resolve as their Apple SDR mezzanine (<footage>/mezz/<stem>.mov, cf.mezz / tools/apple-sdr: AVFoundation's own HDR -> SDR tone mapping, what QuickTime and Photos show), tagged Rec.709 Gamma 2.4, no HLG CDL. 'resolve' imports the HLG file and lets Resolve convert it (one stop brighter and flatter than the Mac shows it). cf.build --hdr-source overrides; --deliver hdr-hlg always uses 'resolve'. ADR 0011.

look.status: no Look since 2026-10-12 (author: original colour, as on the Mac); before that cinema-clean (2026-10-10). cf.build --look <file.cube> still applies one on request
look.brief: rich, saturated, expensive cinematic travel-film image: deep but not crushed shadows, glowing highlights, warm/teal split, skin protected

assets._doc: Library Asset cues (shots[].assets; docs/script-schema.md, Assets). pos boxes are reference px (x, y = top-left), the Asset fits inside the box, centred; 'full' covers the canvas, 'fit' fits it; canvases.landscape.asset_pos holds the 16:9 boxes. Every portrait box lies inside safe_zone and clear of right_rail. still_s is a picture's default length, still_max_s its longest; sfx_free_max_s: a sound effect of unknown rights shorter than this is allowed (with a warning). Level of a sound cue: integrated loudness sfx_below_track_db under the Track (or under audio.target_lufs without one), plus the cue's db, capped by audio.true_peak_dbtp and clamped to gain_range_db. loop_clear_s: on a loop_seamless Reel a picture must end this long before the end.

speech.note: the author films and talks from behind the camera; that is fine (music covers it). Only the person ON camera talking is a reject, until the voiceover phase.

ending.note: every Reel loops: the last shot and the first shot are one continuous action from one clip, split at the seam (author rule, 2026-10-10)

upscale.mode_note: '2x' since 2026-10-11: on reel-01 (4 of 8 shots upscaled) '2x-enhanced' rendered in 314 s vs 47 s for plain 2x, 27 s without Super Scale and 10 s at 1080x1920, over the ~5x budget. sharpness / noise_reduction are only used by '2x-enhanced'. Comparison: reels/reel-01/out/superscale-compare.png in the potsdam-2026-10-04 Footage.
upscale.note: Resolve Studio Super Scale on every source clip whose display height is below canvas.height (the 1080x1920 iPhone clips on a 2160x3840 canvas); clips at or above it get 1 (off). mode '2x-enhanced' = SetClipProperty('Super Scale', 2, sharpness, noise_reduction) with floats 0..1; mode '2x' = SetClipProperty('Super Scale', 2). cf.build --no-superscale sets every clip to 1.

reframe.note: How a landscape clip fills the vertical canvas when a shot has no reframe (cf.reframe): 'follow' = a static 9:16 window on the person (cf.follow: person detector on the proxy, the window that holds the whole person in the most frames, ties toward the end of the shot; never leaves the source, no Tilt). 'smart' (Resolve Smart Reframe) is available per shot but off by default: it tilts past the source edge and leaves black bands (Mallorca reel-01: 692 and 644 px; author: black bars are unacceptable, 2026-10-11).

render.codec_note: H.264 High is the default (Instagram re-encodes everything). GetRenderCodecs('mp4') on this Mac also lists 'H265' (H.265), which would give a smaller file at the same quality; not used, because render_check and the loudness fix expect h264.
render.bitrate_note: VideoQuality cap per canvas (SetRenderSettings VideoQuality = Mbit/s x 1000, kbit/s).
